claims.text: An active-learning-enhanced machine-learning potential coupled with thermodynamic integration can accurately reproduce solid and liquid free energies.
The proposed framework can retain vibrational entropy, anharmonicity, and electron–vibration effects.
The proposed framework will cost substantially less than full ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows.
The proposed framework will scale better than explicit AIMD and TOR-TILD for multicomponent systems.
The ML potential will be iteratively refined using short, on-the-fly ab initio MD calculations.
The refined ML potential will drive thermodynamic-integration calculations across the melting transition.
Triggering active learning when configurations depart from the training domain will ensure sufficient sampling around phase boundaries.
ML-driven MD trajectories will capture anharmonic lattice dynamics and vibrational-entropy contributions.
ML-driven MD trajectories will capture local electron–vibration coupling.
Adding targeted ab initio configurations from critical regions near melting will produce a surrogate that faithfully reproduces the relevant energetic contributions.
The surrogate will avoid the need for long ab initio MD trajectories.
The method is predicted to provide a 5–10-fold computational speed-up relative to explicit AIMD.
The method is predicted to achieve free-energy accuracy within tens of meV per atom.
Phase free-energy differences are predicted to remain within experimental uncertainty.
The intended validated scope includes elemental metals and simple binary alloys near 0.9–1.1 times their melting temperature.
The method may extend to high-entropy alloys if the training dataset is sufficiently comprehensive.
